S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder is characterized by persistent, excessive worry about multiple areas of life that is difficult to control, lasts for months, and is accompanied by physical and cognitive tension such as sleep disturbance, concentration difficulty, and muscle tightness. It typically has a gradual course and becomes clinically significant when the worry extends beyond a specific stressor, impairs functioning, and is not better explained by episodic panic, trauma re-experiencing, mood episodes, or a circumscribed phobia.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Fourteen months before seeking care, Edelmira’s elderly mother moved into her San Antonio home after a fall, turning Edelmira’s carefully structured life into a mix of caregiving, library leadership, grant deadlines, and family obligations. At first she responded in her usual way—calendars, meal plans, yoga, and meticulous contingency lists—but over the year her worry spread from her mother’s safety to work performance, finances, community commitments, and whether she was failing the values of respeto and solidaridad she had grown up with. The worry became difficult to set aside, disrupted her sleep, tightened her shoulders and neck, and increasingly interfered with concentration during cataloging decisions, staff meetings, and digital preservation planning. She finally requested psychiatric care after a grant presentation went poorly because her mind repeatedly went blank, and her primary care physician agreed that the yearlong pattern had become more than ordinary caregiver stress.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: I came in because once a worry starts—about my mother getting up at night, a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—I can’t seem to shelve it in my mind, no matter how many lists I make or how hard I try to redirect myself.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there replaying the day and planning for every possible problem, then if I wake to hear my mother moving around I’m up for an hour or two afterward and arrive at the library feeling like I never really rested.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: Over this past year my worrying has spread from just my mother’s safety to finances, staff decisions, deadlines, the house, and whether I’m being a good daughter, and even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: During cataloging reviews or staff meetings, I’ll be looking right at the screen or the agenda and suddenly realize I haven’t absorbed a word because my mind has wandered into some problem I think I should have prevented.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.
S061.manifestation: By the end of the day my neck and shoulders feel locked up from bracing myself, and I catch myself clenching my jaw while answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started missing small but important details at the library and had to hand off parts of a grant presentation after I froze, which is not like me and has made me worry about whether I can keep leading my team well.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year and two months, since my mother moved into my home after her fall.
